memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The king of Jericho was told, "Look, some of the Israelites have come here tonight to spy out the land." So the king of Jericho sent this message to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, because they have come to spy out the whole land." — Josh 2:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Word travels fast in a frightened city. The king of Jericho hears that Israelite spies have slipped in, and he traces them straight to Rahab's door. Suddenly this woman is caught in the middle of a national crisis, facing the most powerful man in her city. His command is clear: hand the men over.

Here is a moment of decision that many of us face in smaller ways. The pressure comes from above, from authority, from the crowd. Everyone expects you to go along. And in that moment, Rahab has to choose whom she truly fears — the king of Jericho, or the God she has only heard about.

The Bible often shows us that the fear of man is a trap (Prov 29:25). We can be so afraid of what people will think or do that we betray what we know to be right. Rahab stood at that crossroads, and what she chose would change her life forever.

We face the same crossroads whenever following Christ costs us the approval of others. The One who said "do not fear those who kill the body" (Matt 10:28) calls us to fear God above every earthly power — and He gives us the courage to do it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When has pressure from authority or the crowd tempted you to do wrong?
2. Whom do you fear more in the crunch — people, or God?
3. What decision are you facing right now where you must choose whom to obey?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when pressure comes to abandon what is right, help me fear You more than I fear people. Give me courage at the crossroads. Amen.
